name: Strong Curves

card.summary: A glute-focused strength-training book and programme by Bret Contreras, used to build the glutes and lower-body shape through progressive resistance training.
card.aka: Strong Curves: A Woman's Guide to Building a Better Butt and Body

quick.overview:
Strong Curves is a fitness book by trainer Bret Contreras, known as The Glute Guy, with a 2013 launch. It sets out glute-focused resistance training for women, including four 12-week routines for different levels, with chapters on muscle-building science, nutrition and movement patterns.

The appearance goal is a more developed, rounder glute and lower body through hypertrophy training, centred on movements like the hip thrust. Research on glute exercises exists, including electromyography and training studies involving Contreras, though none test the book itself.
quick.how: Readers follow a structured programme of resistance training with glute-emphasis exercises, plus a warm-up, logging workouts and nutrition guidance, across several months.
quick.risks: Resistance training carries ordinary risks of strain and technique-related injury; the book includes technique guidance and an index of over 200 exercises.

lead: Strong Curves: A Woman's Guide to Building a Better Butt and Body is a fitness book by Bret Contreras, who markets himself as The Glute Guy; the author's site announced its launch on 2 April 2013 [1]. It is a glute-focused programme.

According to the author's description, chapters 1 to 9 cover the components of a woman's physique, muscle-building science, nutrition and movement patterns, while chapters 10 to 14 give a warm-up, four 12-week glute-focused routines for different levels, workout logs and lifestyle suggestions, plus an index of more than 200 exercises [1].

The appearance goal is muscle growth in the glutes and lower body. The hip thrust, the exercise most associated with Contreras's work, trains the gluteus maximus [2]. A 2015 study by Contreras and colleagues compared electromyographic activity in the back squat and barbell hip thrust in 13 trained women [3].

angle.text: The programme uses structured weight training, with hip thrusts and other glute-targeting lifts, to build gluteal muscle over 12-week blocks.

paras: The author's page describes the book as a complete guide to building a woman's physique, strength and lifestyle, with a free 46-page sample [1]. These are promotional descriptions by the author.
The hip thrust involves reclining against a surface and lifting the hips with weight on the lap, training the gluteus maximus [2].

No studies of the Strong Curves programme itself were found. Related research includes a 2015 EMG comparison of squat and barbell hip thrust in 13 trained women by Contreras and colleagues [3], and a 2023 trial reporting that hip thrust and back squat training elicited similar gluteus muscle hypertrophy, with Contreras as a co-author [4].

timeline.event: Contreras et al. EMG study of squat and hip thrust [3]
Hip thrust versus squat hypertrophy trial published [4]
